Actual checker independently reconstructs direct geometric chords and evaluates spheroidal/multiaxis/coalescing coefficients with reproducible finite tests.

originality.rationale: The main claim is the nontrivial double-scaling beta crossover of rare Crofton chord length and a coalescing principal axis in dimensions >=4. Heinrich 2014 has general fixed-shape power moments, and Kellerer 1984 has low-dimensional spheroid distributions; neither inspected result states the nonuniform axis-collision limit. The strongest prior implicit fixed-distribution coverage is openly acknowledged; existing moment formulas do not supply the evaluated joint scaling function or its matching constants without new uniform analysis. Historical priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The extreme-chord probability for fixed ellipsoid shapes has a leading-coefficient singularity as principal semiaxes tie. The new theorem resolves this natural critical boundary layer by one explicit strictly decreasing beta profile, all allowable multiplicities, exact dimension-dependent exponents and matching to the neighboring fixed-gap asymptotic. The problem is a natural geometrically motivated degeneracy rather than an arbitrary finite parameter slice or pretabulated moment.
